LOCALISATION. For any path from B(lam*) = Z_{<=-2} u {p} to B(mu*) = Z_{<=-3} u {p, E-2}, p := e_min - 2, no bead at a site <= -3 ever moves and no bead ever lands there. Proof: H_y(B) := #{x <= y : x not in B} is non-decreasing along any sequence of rightward hops and strictly increases exactly when a bead crosses y; H_y = 0 at both ends for every y <= -3, so there are no crossings of any such y. Hence exactly the two beads at -2 and p can move, and the paths split into exactly two sectors: (NC) non-crossing, the upper bead ends at E-2 and the lower at p; (C) crossing, the upper bead never moves and the lower performs all k hops. This is the step that makes a k-fold nested bracket a TWO-BODY problem for every k.

THE MECHANISM, and where the 1+t comes from. Sector (NC): every hop has weight t^0 (the lower bead stays weakly left of p, the upper weakly right, so neither crosses the other), and a word is legal iff the label set Sbar of the lower bead's hops is NOT a time-prefix of the word -- the only failure is the lower bead's last hop landing on p before the upper bead has vacated it. Sector (C): every legal path has weight exactly t^1 (the lower bead crosses p exactly once), and a word is legal iff no partial sum e_{w_1}+...+e_{w_s} equals e_min -- i.e. the lower bead never lands on p. Since the e_i are positive the partial sums are strictly increasing, so each excluded word has a UNIQUE such prefix, and the two exclusion sets carry the SAME signed count X = sum over Sbar with Sigma_Sbar = e_min of N(Sbar). Hence the entry is -X - tX = -X(1+t). NO INVOLUTION is used: the divisibility is the statement that the collision blocking the non-crossing sector is the collision blocking the crossing sector, and 1+t records the two ways two beads may sit around it. Contrast Q83, where 1+t came from a toggling pairing that shifted a threshold by one.

THE SIGN SUM. For nonempty Sbar subset [k], N(Sbar) := sum over w in U (unimodal words with peak k, sign (-1)^{q-1}) whose first |Sbar| letters are exactly Sbar, of eps(w). Then N(Sbar) = (-1)^{|Sbar|} if k-1 in Sbar and k not in Sbar; (-1)^{|Sbar|-1} if k in Sbar and k-1 not in Sbar; and 0 if Sbar contains both or neither. Proof by the rho_T parametrisation (T = letters before the peak, eps = (-1)^{|T|}) in two cases, each collapsing by sum over subsets of a nonempty set of (-1)^{|B|} = 0. Evaluated at Sigma_Sbar = e_min it collapses to a SINGLE set: if e_{k-1} < e_k then k in Sbar is impossible (Sigma >= e_k > e_min) and k-1 in Sbar forces Sbar = {k-1}; symmetrically otherwise. So X = -sgn(e_k - e_{k-1}), with no generating-function coefficient entering -- the choice e_min = min(e_{k-1},e_k), rather than either one separately, is what makes the collapse total.
